To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the particle size of the limestone source fed to broiler breeders had a significant effect on egg quality, but had little effect on P excretion.
particle size effects of calcium sources were found on plasma, excretion and urinary changes in Ca and P of non‐colostomy and colostomy broiler breeders.
the particle size of limestone did not significantly influence P excretion in broiler breder hens, but it did influence the timing in Ca and P excretions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of particle size of calcium on plasma and urinary changes in calcium and phosphorus in broiler breeders.
the effects of dietary calcium particle size on plasma, excrete, and urinary changes of Ca and P.
the effects of particle size of Ca on plasma, excretions and urinary Ca and Ca excretion in broiler breder hens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the particle size of the calcium source (smaller and/or larger) did not significantly influence total Ca and P excretions in the urine but did influence the time of Ca and P secretion.
the particle size of calcium source did influence the timing and magnitude of urinary excretion of both P and Ca in broiler breder hens.
the particle size of the calcium source did not influence the qualitative or quantitative total urinary Ca and P excretions, but it did influence the timing (hours) of Ca and P peak excretions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the smaller particle limestone was more efficient than the larger particle limestone in the retention of P and Ca in tibia ash, egg shell and egg specific gravity, but the differences in the urinary Ca and P excretions between the smaller and larger particle limestone fed groups were not significant.
the particle size effect of the Ca source on P and Ca excretions is dependent on the time after oviposition.
the particle size of calcium source does not significantly influence the total excretion of P but does significantly influence the total Ca excretion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the particle size of Ca source did not influence the total P excretion but did influence the specific gravity and ash content of eggshells.
the particle size of the Ca source did not significantly alter the quantitative urinary excretion of calcium and phosphorus.
the particle size of calcium source does not influence the overall Ca and P excreted in the feces, but the particle size does influence the timing of the excretion.
